# Working brand identity — `UX-BR-01`

Status: candidate. “Engineer Assessment” is a workspace descriptor, not a cleared public name. There is no selected logo, domain or registered mark. Product and research owners must review any public claim and commission a name/rights check before launch.

## Promise and character

The pilot offers an interesting three-case challenge and specific reflection on the submitted answers. It invites curiosity and makes limits visible. The voice is direct, calm, concrete and respectful of uncertainty. The reader should know what action to take, what data will be processed, and what the result can say.

| Context | Candidate copy | Avoid |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Invitation | “Work through three short engineering cases. Each recorded answer is limited to ten minutes.” | “Prove you are a top engineer.” |
| Purpose | “Research use is optional. Your choice does not change access to the offered challenge feedback.” | Bundled or vague “improve our AI” consent. |
| Recording | “Recording started. Your camera preview is visible here. Background blur is on.” | Hidden capture or implied privacy protection from blur alone. |
| Failure | “Upload stopped. Your recorded answer remains on this device while we retry. The session clock will not restart.” | “Something went wrong” with no next action. |
| Feedback | “In this answer, you compared two approaches and left the consistency guarantee unclear.” | “You are a weak architect.” |

Use “case”, “answer”, “evidence”, “feedback” and “practice step” consistently. Explain `NA` as “this case did not fairly test it” and `UNK` as “the evidence could not be reviewed”; never display either as zero. Do not call the feedback a job match, talent score, personality result, honesty score or hiring verdict.

## Visual direction and asset rules

Use the warm off-white and dark ink from [tokens](tokens.json) for reading; blue identifies primary actions, amber warns about a recoverable concern, and red signals blocking failure. Status text always accompanies color. Use simple diagrams of reasoning or product work only when they clarify a case; avoid stock interview imagery, faces as credibility signals, badges of ability and surveillance motifs. The mark, if later commissioned, needs a monochrome variant, small-size test, accessible text fallback, clearance and recorded owner Decision. Case content itself should not depend on brand color or illustration.

Before release, test name/claim comprehension with intended users, review copy for language and access needs, and version every public surface using the selected notice and claim tier. Positive feedback about the look does not validate assessment scores.
